paragraphs: Evommune is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing innovative therapies that target key drivers of chronic inflammatory diseases, with initial clinical development programs focusing on chronic spontaneous urticaria ("CSU"), atopic dermatitis ("AD") and ulcerative colitis ("UC"). Chronic inflammation is a significant healthcare problem in the world, substantially impacting patients' quality of life and leading to life-threatening conditions. These conditions, if not prevented, ultimately lead to fatal diseases, such as cardiovascular diseases, diabetes and cancer, which contribute to three out of every five deaths worldwide and result in an estimated $90 billion of annual cost to the healthcare system in the United States.

Our mission is to improve patients' daily lives and prevent the long-term effects of uncontrolled inflammation that are a consequence of the limitations of existing therapies. To achieve this, we are advancing a portfolio of differentiated product candidates that target key drivers of chronic inflammation.

Our management team's proven drug development expertise and experience in the field of immunology and inflammation, combined with advanced scientific tools, enable us to identify and advance potent, highly selective molecules with distinctive mechanisms of action. By identifying treatment gaps of chronic inflammatory diseases, we strive to transform the treatment landscape, developing therapies that have the potential to offer rapid symptom relief and provide safe, durable resolution of the underlying disease. Among our portfolio of programs, we currently have two product candidates, EVO756 and EVO301, in Phase 2 development. We are initially developing EVO756 for the treatment of CSU and AD, and EVO301 for the treatment of AD and UC. We see broad expansion potential for both programs across additional chronic inflammatory diseases. We also intend to advance additional preclinical programs into clinical development.

Our most advanced clinical-stage product candidate, EVO756, is a potent and highly selective oral small molecule antagonist of MRGPRX2, a receptor predominantly found on mast cells and peripheral sensory neurons. Dysregulated MRGPRX2 activity can play a key role as both a catalyst and perpetuator of disease pathogenesis across a multitude of systemic chronic inflammatory diseases. By targeting MRGPRX2, we believe EVO756 is the only dual mechanism clinical approach that modulates both mast cells and peripheral sensory neurons, representing a new potential therapeutic option to reduce inflammation and provide rapid relief of itch (pruritus). Mast cells are critical regulators of immune response and can be found in most vascularized tissues including skin, lung and the digestive tract. These cells tend to be distributed in close proximity to peripheral sensory neurons, where the activation of the neurons can trigger the inflammatory cascade and mast cells are implicated in further perpetuating neuroinflammation and its related symptoms. We believe MRGPRX2 is the only clinical approach aimed at inhibiting this neuroimmune interaction.

We previously announced the topline results from a Phase 1 proof-of-concept trial in 132 healthy volunteers designed to assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic ("PK") properties and pharmacodynamic ("PD") properties of orally administered EVO756. Comprehensive trial results were presented at the UCARE Global Urticaria Forum meeting in December 2024. EVO756 was observed to be well-tolerated at all doses tested, with no serious adverse events ("SAEs"), and PK results supporting daily dosing. A skin challenge test was also conducted in the multiple ascending dose ("MAD") portion of the trial in which icatibant, a known MRGPRX2 ligand, representative of a broad class of disease relevant ligands, was administered via intradermal injection to healthy volunteers creating measurable wheals on their skin. EVO756 was observed to robustly decrease the healthy volunteers' wheals induced by icatibant, evidencing meaningful target engagement at all doses tested. We are currently conducting a Phase 2b trial of EVO756 in CSU and have completed a Phase 2 trial of EVO756 in chronic inducible urticaria ("CIndU" and together with CSU, chronic urticarias or "CU").

In May 2025, we reported topline results from our U.S. multicenter Phase 2 trial of EVO756 in CIndU that demonstrated clinical activity (including improvement in FricTest score and pruritus numerical rating score ("pruritus-NRS"), as described below) in a patient population with symptomatic dermographism. The trial was designed to generate additional patient data in a population with symptomatic dermographism, which we believe is highly translatable to the CSU patient population due to overlapping disease biology and shared pathophysiology. Third party trials have demonstrated that symptomatic dermographism affects approximately 25% of the CSU patient population; similarly, we believe EVO756's clinical activity in symptomatic dermographism patients strongly supports the role of MRGPRX2 in neurogenic inflammation, which plays a crucial role in AD.

A total of 30 patients were enrolled in the trial, with 11 patients enrolled in the 300 mg once daily ("QD") cohort and 19 patients enrolled in the 50 mg twice daily ("BID") cohort. Rapid clinical activity was observed in both dosing regimens, with some patients demonstrating responses by week one in both FricTest score (a clinician-rated measure of symptomatic dermographism severity ranging from 0 to 4, with higher scores indicating greater severity) and pruritus-NRS. 70% (n=19) of the 27 observed patients demonstrated improvement at just four weeks, with 30% (n=8) of the observed patients achieving a complete response (achieving a FricTest score of zero), of which 50% were immunoglobulin E ("IgE") high (as defined by a serum IgE level of ≥100 IU/mL). An additional 11% (n=3) achieved a partial response as defined by a ≥2-point decrease in FricTest score and a further 30% (n=8) demonstrated a one-point decrease in FricTest score. The population of subjects observed at four weeks does not include three patients who were unevaluable or lost to follow-up. Observed patients in the 300 mg QD cohort saw an average reduction of 1.4 points in FricTest score after four weeks and observed patients in the 50 mg BID cohort saw an average reduction of 1.5 points. By comparison, in separate, independent trials conducted by third parties, patients treated with 300 mg omalizumab saw a reduction of 1.4 points and patients treated with 300 mg barzolvolimab saw a reduction of 1.6 points in FricTest score after four weeks. EVO756 was observed to be well-tolerated at both dose levels, including the higher 300 mg QD dose. No SAEs were observed and there were no discontinuations due to adverse events ("AEs").

We initiated a Phase 2b dose-ranging trial in CSU in April 2025 and expect to report initial results in the second quarter of 2026. We also initiated a Phase 2b dose-ranging trial in moderate-to-severe AD patients in August 2025 and expect to report initial results in the second half of 2026. We plan to evaluate EVO756 in additional indications in which mast cell degranulation and neuroinflammation are key drivers of disease, with migraine being our next indication of interest where we plan to initiate a Phase 2b trial in mid-2026.

Our second clinical-stage product candidate, EVO301, is a long-acting fusion protein consisting of an IL-18 binding protein ("BP") and an anti-serum albumin Fab-associated ("SAFA") domain. IL-18 is a pro-inflammatory cytokine of the IL-1 family that regulates various immune processes that drive inflammation and is a potent modulator of ongoing inflammation. The IL-18 pathway is believed to play a key role in the severity and progression of several large, highly prevalent chronic inflammatory disease populations with a significant number of uncontrolled patients, including AD and UC. The SAFA domain incorporated into EVO301 utilizes neonatal fragment crystallizable receptor ("FcRn")-mediated recycling of serum albumin to extend half-life. We believe EVO301's optimized approach to IL-18 binding and neutralization could enable significant advantages and differentiated clinical outcomes for patients, including with respect to efficacy, tissue distribution, dosing profile and reduced immunogenicity risk. In addition, EVO301's distinct mechanism and modality complement those of EVO756, providing us with multiple potential avenues to bring innovative therapeutics to the large, underserved and rapidly expanding population of patients suffering from chronic inflammatory diseases.

In February 2026, we announced positive top-line results from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2a trial evaluating EVO301 in adult patients with moderate-to-severe AD. The trial met its primary efficacy endpoint at week 12 and achieved highly statistically significant outcomes in adult patients with moderate-to-severe AD. The 70-patient trial was designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of intravenous dosing of 5 mg/kg on day 1 and day 28 (n=48 active, n=22 placebo) over 12 weeks. The trial met its primary endpoint, demonstrating clinically meaningful activity in AD with statistical significance over placebo achieved at weeks 4, 8 and 12 at p<0.01. We believe demonstrating this activity with an IL-18 targeting therapy supports the relevance of this pathway in disease pathophysiology and reinforces that pathways beyond classic Th2 biology can contribute meaningfully to disease activity. Expanding therapeutics to target novel mechanisms like IL 18 could offer benefit for patients who remain uncontrolled on existing therapies and reinforces the urgent need to develop more options across the growing AD population. We plan to rapidly move a subcutaneous formulation of EVO301 into a Phase 2b trial in AD where we believe optimized and more frequent dosing of EVO301 could achieve potential best-in-class Eczema Area and Severity Index ("EASI") activity.

Beyond AD, we are evaluating a potential Phase 2 trial in moderate-to-severe UC patients. We may also evaluate EVO301 in Crohn's disease, certain cardiovascular-related inflammatory conditions, and other additional indications, in which dysregulation of the IL-18 pathway contributes to chronic inflammation and tissue damage driving disease pathology. Notes: (1) Other potential indications for EVO756 include asthma, interstitial cystitis, irritable bowel syndrome and pruritus. To date, based on our data from the successful completion of our Phase 1 proof-of-concept trial of EVO756 in healthy volunteers, we believe there is a path to proceed to Phase 2 clinical development for these other indications, similar to our initiation of our Phase 2b trial in AD, subject to standard regulatory requirements. (2) We are currently prioritizing development in other indications ahead of CIndU and may conduct additional CIndU trials in the future.

In addition to our clinical programs, we are advancing a pipeline of preclinical candidates for immunology and inflammation indications and aim to deliver a steady cadence of data for our new programs.

Collectively, our team members have held leadership roles at over 25 companies and have played key roles in the discovery and development of nearly 30 approved small molecules and biologics, primarily in immunology and inflammation, including Ebglyss (lebrikizumab), Cimzia (certolizumab pegol) and Rezurock (belumosudil). These therapies have significantly impacted patient outcomes, generated billions of dollars in sales and have led to multiple company acquisitions. This experience has informed our approach to drug development and commercialization to become one focused on identifying the areas of highest unmet need in chronic inflammatory diseases, identifying the molecules with the highest probability of improving patient outcomes in those diseases and then advancing our molecules through rigorous and thoughtful development programs.

headings: Risks Related to Our Limited Operating History, Financial Position and Capital Requirements
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our stockholders and may restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our product candidates.
Risks Related to Discovery, Development and Regulatory Approval of Product Candidates
If we do not achieve our projected development goals in the time frames we announce and expect, the commercialization of our therapeutics may be delayed and, as a result, our stock price may decline.

Obtaining and maintaining marketing approval of our product candidates in one jurisdiction does not mean that we will be successful in obtaining marketing approval of our product candidates in other jurisdictions.
We may develop our current or future product candidates in combination with other therapies, which would expose us to additional risks.

paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. Before deciding to invest in shares of our common stock, you should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and their related notes included elsewhere herein and the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations." If any of the following risks actually occurs, our business, prospects, operating results and financial condition could suffer materially, the trading price of our common stock could decline and you could lose all or part of your investment. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial also may materially and adversely affect our business, prospects, operating results and financial condition.

We have a limited operating history and no products approved for commercial sale, which may make it difficult to evaluate our current business and predict our future success and viability. We have incurred net losses in every year since our inception. We expect to continue to incur net losses in the future.

We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company with a limited operating history. Since our inception in 2020, we have invested most of our resources in developing our product candidates, building our intellectual property portfolio, conducting business planning, organizing and staffing our company, raising capital, conducting preclinical studies and, more recently, clinical trials and providing general and administrative support for these operations. Biopharmaceutical product development is a highly speculative undertaking, involving substantial upfront capital expenditure and significant risk. Any product candidate may fail to demonstrate adequate efficacy or an acceptable safety profile, gain regulatory approval or become commercially viable, despite substantial investment on development or commercialization. To date, Evommune has not yet demonstrated its ability to successfully obtain regulatory approvals, manufacture a product on a commercial scale, or arrange for a third party to do so on its behalf, or conduct sales and marketing activities necessary for successful commercialization. Consequently, predictions about our future success or viability may not be as accurate as they could be if Evommune had a longer operating history or a history of successfully developing and commercializing biopharmaceutical products. We continue to incur significant research and development and other expenses related to our ongoing operations. As a result, we are not profitable and have incurred losses in each year since our inception. For the year ended December 31, 2025, we had a net loss of $68.9 million. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $221.1 million. We expect to continue to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future and expect these losses to increase as we continue our research and development of, and seek regulatory approvals for, our two clinical-stage product candidates, EVO756 and EVO301, along with any future product candidates we may develop.
We anticipate that our expenses will increase substantially if, and as, we:

• continue the research and development of our clinical- and preclinical-stage product candidates and discovery-stage programs, including the continued development of our most advanced product candidates, EVO756 and EVO301;
• increase the amount of research and development activities to identify and develop product candidates to advance into clinical trial development;

In addition, if and when we seek and obtain regulatory approval to commercialize any product candidate, we will also incur increased expenses in connection with commercialization and marketing of any such product. paragraphs: Evommune 是一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，開發創新療法，針對慢性發炎性疾病的主要驅動因素，初期臨牀開發計畫著重於慢性自發性蕁麻疹（"CSU"）、過敏性濕疹（"AD"）及潰瘍性結腸炎（"UC"）。慢性發炎是全球重要的醫療問題，顯著影響患者的生存品質，並導致致命性病症。若未加以預防，這些病症最終會導致致命性疾病，例如心血管疾病、糖尿病及癌症，這些疾病佔全球每五個死亡案例中的三個，並導致美國醫療系統每年產生約 90 十億美元的費用。
我們的使命是改善患者的日常生活，並預防現有療法侷限所導致的未控制發炎的長期影響。為達成此目標，我們正在推進一組差異化的產品候選藥物，這些藥物針對慢性發炎的主要驅動因素。

我們管理團隊在藥物開發領域的已證實專業經驗，以及在免疫學和發炎領域的經驗，結合先進的科學工具，使我們能夠識別並推進強效且高度選擇性的分子，具有獨特的作用機制。透過識別慢性發炎性疾病治療的缺口，我們致力於改變治療景觀，開發具有潛力提供快速症狀緩解，並提供安全、持久的疾病根本解決方案的療法。在我們的產品計畫中，目前我們有兩種產品候選藥物，EVO756 和 EVO301，處於第二期臨牀開發階段。我們最初將 EVO756 用於治療 CSU 和 AD，將 EVO301 用於治療 AD 和 UC。我們認為這兩個計畫在其他慢性發炎性疾病中也有廣泛的擴展潛力。我們也計畫將其他前期研究計畫推進至臨牀開發階段。

我們最進展的臨牀階段產品候選藥物 EVO756，是一種強效且高度選擇性的口服小分子 MRGPRX2 受體拮抗劑，MRGPRX2 受體主要分佈在肥大細胞和周圍感測神經元上。MRGPRX2 活性失調可能在多種系統性慢性發炎性疾病中扮演催化劑和持續發病機制的角色。透過針對 MRGPRX2，我們認為 EVO756 是唯一同時作用於肥大細胞和周圍感測神經元的雙重機制臨牀方法，代表一種新的潛在治療選擇，以減少發炎並提供快速的癢（pruritus）緩解。肥大細胞是免疫反應的關鍵調節者，可見於大多數血管化組織，包括皮膚、肺部和消化道。這些細胞通常分佈在周圍感測神經元附近，其中神經元的活化會觸發發炎 cascade，而肥大細胞被認為進一步持續神經發炎及其相關症狀。我們認為 MRGPRX2 是唯一針對抑制這種神經免疫互動的臨牀方法。

我們先前宣佈了在 132 名健康志願者中進行的 Phase 1 證實概念試驗的初步結果，試驗旨在評估口服 EVO756 的安全性、耐受性、藥動學（"PK"）特性及藥效學（"PD"）特性。綜合試驗結果在 2024 年 12 月的 UCARE 全球蕁麻疹論壇會議中發表。EVO756 在所有測試劑量下均被觀察為耐受良好，無嚴重不良事件（"SAEs"），且藥動學結果支持每日給藥。在多劑量（"MAD"）部分的試驗中，也進行了皮膚挑戰測試，其中 icatibant（已知的 MRGPRX2 配體，代表一類廣泛疾病相關配體）經皮下注射至健康志願者，導致其皮膚產生可測量的風團。觀察到 EVO756 在所有測試劑量下均能顯著減少由 icatibant 引起的健康志願者的風團，顯示出目標參與的意義。我們目前正在進行 EVO756 在 CSU 的 Phase 2b 試驗，並已完成 EVO756 在慢性誘發性蕁麻疹（"CIndU"）的 Phase 2 試驗（與 CSU 合併稱為慢性蕁麻疹或 "CU"）。

2025 年 5 月，我們報告了在美國多中心 Phase 2 試驗中 EVO756 在 CIndU 的初步結果，顯示在有症狀的皮膚劃痕症患者中具有臨牀活性（包括 FricTest 分數改善及癢數值評分（"pruritus-NRS"）改善，如後文所述）。試驗設計旨在產生更多患者數據，以評估有症狀的皮膚劃痕症患者羣體，我們認為此羣體與 CSU 患者羣體具有高度可轉化性，因兩者有重疊的疾病生物學和共享的病理生理學。第三方試驗顯示，有症狀的皮膚劃痕症約影響 CSU 患者羣體的 25%；同樣地，我們認為 EVO756 在有症狀的皮膚劃痕症患者的臨牀活性，強化了 MRGPRX2 在神經性發炎中的作用，而神經性發炎在 AD 中扮演關鍵角色。

總共 30 名患者參與試驗，其中 11 名參與 300 mg 一日一次（"QD"）組，19 名參與 50 mg 一日兩次（"BID"）組。兩種劑量方案均觀察到快速的臨牀活性，部分患者在第一週即顯示 FricTest 分數（評估有症狀的皮膚劃痕症嚴重程度的臨牀評估指標，範圍為 0 到 4，分數越高表示嚴重程度越高）及 pruritus-NRS 的改善。27 名觀察到的患者中，70%（n=19）在四週內顯示改善，其中 30%（n=8）的觀察到患者達到完全反應（FricTest 分數為零），其中 50% 的患者為免疫球蛋白 E（"IgE"）高（定義為血清 IgE 水平 ≥100 IU/mL）。另外 11%（n=3）的患者達到部分反應，定義為 FricTest 分數減少 ≥2 分，另有 30%（n=8）的患者 FricTest 分數減少 1 分。在四週觀察到的患者中，不包括三名未評估或失聯的患者。300 mg QD 組觀察到的患者在四週後 FricTest 分數平均減少 1.4 分，50 mg BID 組觀察到的患者在四週後 FricTest 分數平均減少 1.5 分。相較之下，在第三方進行的獨立試驗中，接受 300 mg omalizumab 治療的患者在四週後 FricTest 分數減少 1.4 分，接受 300 mg barzolvolimab 治療的患者在四週後 FricTest 分數減少 1.6 分。EVO756 在兩種劑量下均被觀察為耐受良好，包括較高的 300 mg QD 劑量。未觀察到 SAEs，也沒有因不良事件（"AEs"）而中止治療。

我們於 2025 年 4 月啟動了 CSU 的 Phase 2b 劑量範圍試驗，預計在 2026 年第二季報告初步結果。我們也於 2025 年 8 月啟動了中度至嚴重 AD 患者的 Phase 2b 劑量範圍試驗，預計在 2026 年下半年報告初步結果。我們計畫評估 EVO756 在其他疾病中，其中肥大細胞去顆粒化和神經發炎是疾病的主要驅動因素，其中偏頭痛是我們接下來的目標適應症，我們預計在 2026 年中啟動 Phase 2b 試驗。

本公司第二階段臨牀產品候選藥物 EVO301 是一種長效融合蛋白，由 IL-18 結合蛋白（"BP"）與抗血清白蛋白 Fab 相關（"SAFA"）結構域組成。IL-18 是 IL-1 家族中一種促發炎性細胞激素，會調控多種免疫過程，驅動發炎，並為持續發炎提供強效調節作用。IL-18 途徑被認為在多種大規模、高度普遍的慢性發炎疾病族羣中扮演關鍵角色，這些疾病族羣中有大量未受控制的患者，包括過敏性皮膚炎（AD）與潰瘍性結腸炎（UC）。EVO301 所整合的 SAFA 結構域利用新生兒片段晶體化受體（"FcRn"）所介導的血清白蛋白回收，以延長半衰期。本公司相信 EVO301 對 IL-18 結合與中和的優化方法，可能為患者帶來顯著優勢與差異化的臨牀結果，包括在療效、組織分佈、給藥特性與降低免疫原性風險方面。此外，EVO301 獨特的機制與模式與 EVO756 相輔相成，為本公司提供多種潛在途徑，以將創新療法帶給受慢性發炎疾病影響的大量未被滿足且快速成長的患者族羣。

2026 年 2 月，本公司宣佈在成人中度至重度過敏性皮膚炎（AD）患者中評估 EVO301 的隨機雙盲安慰劑對照第二期 a 期試驗取得正面的初步結果。試驗在第 12 週達成主要療效終點，並在成人中度至重度 AD 患者中取得高度統計顯著的結果。該 70 位患者的試驗設計用以評估在第 1 天與第 28 天以 5 mg/kg 經靜脈注射給藥（n=48 活躍組，n=22 安慰劑組）持續 12 週的安全性與療效。試驗達成主要終點，顯示在 AD 患者中具有臨牀意義的療效，並在第 4、第 8 與第 12 週對安慰劑取得統計顯著結果（p<0.01）。本公司相信顯示此療效的 IL-18 目標治療，支持此途徑在疾病病態學中的相關性，並強化了除經典 Th2 生物學之外的其他途徑對疾病活動的有意義貢獻。拓展針對新機制如 IL-18 的療法，可能為仍在現有療法中未受控制的患者帶來益處，並強化開發更多選擇以應對不斷成長的 AD 族羣的迫切需求。本公司計畫迅速將 EVO301 的皮下劑型投入 AD 的第二期 b 期試驗，我們相信優化且更頻繁的 EVO301 給藥可能實現潛在最佳等級的濕疹面積與嚴重度指數（"EASI"）療效。
除了 AD 之外，本公司正在評估在中度至重度潰瘍性結腸炎（UC）患者中進行第二期試驗的潛在可能。本公司也可能評估 EVO301 在克羅恩病、某些心血管相關發炎疾病，以及其他附加適應症中的應用，其中 IL-18 途徑的異常調節會導致慢性發炎與組織損傷，驅動疾病病態學。下圖提供本公司目前臨牀開發路線圖的概覽：

說明：(1) EVO756 的其他潛在適應症包括氣喘、間質性膀胱炎、腸易激綜合症與癢症。截至目前為止，根據本公司在健康志願者中成功完成 EVO756 第一期概念驗證試驗的數據，本公司認為有路徑可進行這些其他適應症的第二期臨牀開發，與本公司在 AD 中啟動第二期 b 期試驗的方式相似，但需符合標準的監管要求。(2) 目前本公司優先開發其他適應症，而非 CIndU，並可能在未來進行額外的 CIndU 試驗。
除了臨牀開發計畫，本公司正在推動免疫學與發炎相關的前期候選藥物開發，並計畫為新開發的計畫提供穩定的數據更新頻率。

總體而言，本公司團隊成員曾在超過 25 家公司擔任領導職務，並在近 30 種已核准的小分子藥物與生物製劑的發現與開發中發揮關鍵角色，主要集中在免疫學與發炎領域，包括 Ebglyss（lebrikizumab）、Cimzia（certolizumab pegol）與 Rezurock（belumosudil）。這些療法已顯著改善患者結果，產生數十億美元的銷售收入，並促成多家公司的收購。這段經驗已影響本公司在藥物開發與商業化方面的策略，使其專注於識別慢性發炎疾病中未被滿足的最高需求領域，識別最有可能改善這些疾病患者結果的分子，並透過嚴謹且深思熟慮的開發計畫推進本公司分子的發展。

paragraphs: 本年度報表（Form 10-K）中，除非另有說明或語境另有要求，否則提及「本公司」、「Evommune」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們的」均指 Evommune, Inc. 以及其合併子公司。您應配合本年度報表（Form 10-K）中財務報表及相關附註，閱讀我們財務狀況與營運成果之分析與討論。部分資訊包含於本討論與分析或本年度報表其他處，包括有關我們業務計畫與策略及相關資金安排之資訊，均為展望性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。由於許多因素，包括本年度報表（Form 10-K）中「風險因素」部分所列因素，我們實際結果可能與本討論與分析中所描述或暗示之展望性陳述有重大差異。
Evommune 為一臨牀階段生物科技公司，開發創新療法，針對慢性發炎疾病之關鍵驅動因素，初期臨牀開發計畫聚焦於慢性自發性蕁麻疹（"CSU"）、過敏性濕疹（"AD"）及潰瘍性結腸炎（"UC"）。慢性發炎為全球重大醫療問題，顯著影響患者生活品質，並導致生命威脅性狀況。
我們的使命為改善患者日常生活的品質，並預防現有療法限制所導致之未控制發炎之長期影響。為達成此目標，我們正在推進一組差異化產品候選藥物，針對慢性發炎之關鍵驅動因素。
在我們的產品計畫中，目前我們有兩種產品候選藥物，EVO756 與 EVO301，處於第二階段臨牀開發。我們最初開發 EVO756 用於治療 CSU 與 AD，EVO301 用於治療 AD 與 UC。我們認為這兩個計畫在其他慢性發炎疾病中具有廣泛擴展潛力。我們也計畫將其他前期研究計畫推進至臨牀開發。
我們於 2020 年 4 月根據特拉華州法律成立，公司名稱為 "Evommune, Inc." 我們有兩家 wholly owned 子公司：Evommune Research, LLC 與 Evommune Biologics, LLC。

自我們成立以來，我們每年均產生顯著之營運虧損。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們累計虧損為 221.1 百萬美元。我們預期在可預見的未來持續產生淨虧損，且我們的研究與開發費用、一般及行政費用與資本支出將持續增加。特別是，我們預期費用將因我們持續開發產品候選藥物，並尋求其監管批准，以及聘僱更多員工、支付外部顧問、律師與會計師費用，以及作為上市公司所產生之其他增加成本而增加。此外，若我們尋求並取得任何產品候選藥物之監管批准以進行商業化，我們亦將因商業化與行銷任何該產品而產生增加費用。我們之淨虧損可能因臨牀試驗時程與其他研究與開發活動之支出而顯著波動，每季每季或每年皆可能不同。
我們預期在接下來幾年持續產生顯著且增加之淨營運虧損，因我們：
• 繼續進行臨牀階段與前期研究階段產品候選藥物與發現階段計畫之研究與開發，包括持續開發我們最進展之產品候選藥物，EVO756 與 EVO301；
• 增加研究與開發活動的金額，以識別並開發產品候選品項；
• 支付里程碑、版稅或其他金額，根據授權或合作協議；• 維護、擴充並保護我們的智慧財產權組合；
• 擴充我們的運營、財務及管理系統，並增加人力，包括支持我們臨牀開發、製造及商業化工作的專員；
• 建立銷售、行銷及分銷基礎設施，以商業化我們可能取得上市許可的任何產品，並打算自行或與第三方合作進行商業化；
• 應對任何競爭性療法及市場發展；• 遭遇作為上市公司運作的額外成本；
• 投資或授權取得其他技術；

headings: 與本公司有限營運歷史、財務狀況及資金需求相關之風險
籌措額外資金可能會導致股東持股稀釋，並可能限制本公司營運或要求本公司放棄對產品候選藥物之權利。
與產品候選藥物之發現、開發及監管審批相關之風險
若本公司未能在所公告及預期之時間內達成預設之開發目標，則本公司之療法產品之商業化可能會延遲，因而導致本公司股票價格下跌。
在某一管轄區取得並維持產品候選藥物之市場許可批准，並不表示本公司將能在其他管轄區成功取得市場許可批准。
本公司可能在開發現有或未來之產品候選藥物時，與其他療法結合使用，此舉將使本公司面臨額外之風險。
美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）及任何相應之外國監管機關，可能不接受在該管轄區以外之地區進行之試驗資料。
與本公司產品候選藥物之商業化、行銷及競爭相關之風險
paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及高度風險。在決定投資本公司普通股之前，您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告表10-K中所有其他資訊，包括我們的合併財務報表及其相關附註，以及標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」的章節。若任何上述風險實際發生，將可能對我們的業務、前景、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大影響，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或認為不重要，也可能對我們的業務、前景、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。
我們擁有有限的營運歷史，且尚未有產品獲得商業銷售批准，這可能使評估我們目前的業務與預測未來的成功與生存能力變得困難。自我們成立以來，我們每年均產生淨虧損。我們預期未來仍將持續產生淨虧損。

本公司為一家臨牀階段生技公司，具有有限的營運歷史。自2020年成立以來，本公司已將大部分資源投入於產品候選藥物的開發、智慧財產權組合的建立、商業計畫的制定、公司組織與人力的組建、資金籌措、進行臨牀前研究，以及近期的臨牀試驗，並提供一般及行政支援以支應這些營運活動。生技藥物的開發是一項高度風險的投資，涉及大量的前期資金支出與重大風險。任何產品候選藥物可能無法顯示足夠的療效或可接受的安全性，或取得監管核准或成為商業可行的產品，即使已投入大量資金於開發或商業化。截至目前為止，Evommune尚未展現其成功取得監管核准、進行商業規模製造或委請第三方代為製造，或進行銷售與行銷活動以實現成功商業化的能力。因此，對本公司未來成功或存續的預測可能不如Evommune擁有較長營運歷史或成功開發與商業化生技藥物的歷史時準確。本公司持續產生與持續營運相關的重大研究與開發及其他費用。因此，本公司尚未獲利，且自成立以來每年均產生虧損。截至2025年12月31日，本公司淨虧損為68.9 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為221.1 百萬美元。本公司預期將持續產生重大虧損，且在可預見的未來，這些虧損將因本公司持續進行產品候選藥物的研發，以及尋求監管核准，包括本公司兩項臨牀階段產品候選藥物EVO756與EVO301，以及任何未來可能開發的產品候選藥物而增加。
我們預期，若我們：
• 繼續研究與開發我們的臨牀與臨牀前階段產品候選品與發現階段計畫，包括持續開發我們最進展的產品候選品EVO756與EVO301；
• 增加研究與開發活動的規模，以識別與開發產品候選品，使其進展至臨牀試驗階段；
